question:
On May 20, 2026, Meta began notifying approximately 8,000 employees — roughly 10% of its global workforce — that their jobs were gone. Singapore employees found out by email at 4 a.m. North American workers were told to stay home and wait. And according to multiple reports from current and former employees, Meta had also been tracking keystrokes and mouse movements to train its AI models. One anonymous employee described it simply: "training your replacement." 
Was Meta's conduct ethically defensible by the standards of responsible corporate conduct? YES or NO.
